sanskrit: ekacchatrā mahī yasya praṇatā hy abhavat purā yo 'śvamedhasahasreṇa tarpayām āsa devatāḥ
english: He to whom the whole earth bowed in submission of old, beneath a single royal canopy, and who gratified the gods with a thousand horse-sacrifices —

sanskrit: yaḥ prādāt kāñcanastambhaṃ prāsādaṃ sarvakāñcanam pūrṇaṃ padmadalākṣīṇāṃ strīṇāṃ śayanasaṃkulam
english: who bestowed a palace of golden pillars, all of gold, thronged with couches and filled with women whose eyes were like the petals of the lotus —

sanskrit: dvijātibhyo 'nurūpebhyaḥ kāmān uccāvacāṃs tathā yasyādeśena tad vittaṃ vyabhajanta dvijātayaḥ
english: who granted to the worthy twice-born their desires both great and small, so that at his command the brāhmaṇas divided that wealth among themselves —

sanskrit: khānayām āsa yaḥ kopāt pṛthivīṃ sāgarāṅkitām yasya nāmnā samudraś ca sāgaratvam upāgataḥ
english: who in his wrath caused the earth to be dug out, marking it with the sea, and from whose name the great water itself came to be called the ocean —

sanskrit: sa cen mamāra sṛñjaya caturbhadrataras tvayā putrāt puṇyataraś caiva mā putram anutapyathāḥ
english: if even he died, O Sṛñjaya — he far richer than you in the four blessings and far more meritorious than your son — then grieve not for your son.

sanskrit: rājānaṃ ca pṛthuṃ vainyaṃ mṛtaṃ śuśruma sṛñjaya yam abhyaṣiñcan saṃbhūya mahāraṇye maharṣayaḥ
english: We have heard, O Sṛñjaya, that King Pṛthu, son of Vena, has died — he whom the great seers assembled together to consecrate in the vast forest.

sanskrit: prathayiṣyati vai lokān pṛthur ity eva śabditaḥ kṣatāc ca nas trāyatīti sa tasmāt kṣatriyaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: "He shall make the worlds prosper" — thus was he proclaimed Pṛthu; and "he saves us from harm" — therefore is he remembered as kṣatriya.

sanskrit: pṛthuṃ vainyaṃ prajā dṛṣṭvā raktāḥ smeti yad abruvan tato rājeti nāmāsya anurāgād ajāyata
english: When the people beheld Pṛthu, son of Vena, they cried, "We are won to him in love"; and so, out of that devotion, the name rājan arose for him.

sanskrit: akṛṣṭapacyā pṛthivī puṭake puṭake madhu sarvā droṇadughā gāvo vainyasyāsan praśāsataḥ
english: While the son of Vena ruled, the earth yielded grain unploughed, honey filled cup upon cup, and the cows gave milk by the droṇa-measure.

sanskrit: arogāḥ sarvasiddhārthā manuṣyā akutobhayāḥ yathābhikāmam avasan kṣetreṣu ca gṛheṣu ca
english: Free of disease, all their aims fulfilled, and afraid of nothing, men dwelt as they desired, in the fields and in their homes.

sanskrit: āpaḥ saṃstambhire yasya samudrasya yiyāsataḥ saritaś cānudīryanta dhvajasaṅgaś ca nābhavat
english: When he wished to cross the sea, its waters stood still; the rivers did not heave up against him, and his banner met no hindrance.

sanskrit: hairaṇyāṃs trinalotsedhān parvatān ekaviṃśatim brāhmaṇebhyo dadau rājā yo 'śvamedhe mahāmakhe
english: In the great rite of the horse-sacrifice that king gave to the brāhmaṇas one and twenty mountains of gold, each three reeds in height.

sanskrit: sa cen mamāra sṛñjaya caturbhadrataras tvayā putrāt puṇyataraś caiva mā putram anutapyathāḥ
english: If even he died, O Sṛñjaya — he far richer than you in the four blessings and far more meritorious than your son — then grieve not for your son.

sanskrit: kiṃ vai tūṣṇīṃ dhyāyasi sṛñjaya tvaṃ; na me rājan vācam imāṃ śṛṇoṣi na cen moghaṃ vipralaptaṃ mayedaṃ; pathyaṃ mumūrṣor iva samyag uktam
english: Why do you brood in silence, O Sṛñjaya? Do you not, O king, hear these words of mine? If you do, then my speech has not been uttered in vain — wholesome counsel rightly spoken, as if to one about to die.

sanskrit: sṛñjaya uvāca śṛṇomi te nārada vācam etāṃ; vicitrārthāṃ srajam iva puṇyagandhām rājarṣīṇāṃ puṇyakṛtāṃ mahātmanāṃ; kīrtyā yuktāṃ śokanirṇāśanārtham
english: Sṛñjaya said: I do hear this speech of yours, O Nārada — rich in wondrous meaning, fragrant with holiness like a garland — a recital, bright with their fame, of those great-souled royal sages and doers of holy deeds, told to dispel my grief.

sanskrit: na te moghaṃ vipralaptaṃ maharṣe; dṛṣṭvaiva tvāṃ nāradāhaṃ viśokaḥ śuśrūṣe te vacanaṃ brahmavādin; na te tṛpyāmy amṛtasyeva pānāt
english: Not in vain have you spoken, O great seer; at the mere sight of you, Nārada, my sorrow is gone. I long to hear your words, O speaker of the sacred truth; I cannot have my fill of them, as of a draught of the nectar of immortality.

sanskrit: amoghadarśin mama cet prasādaṃ; sutāghadagdhasya vibho prakuryāḥ mṛtasya saṃjīvanam adya me syāt; tava prasādāt sutasaṃgamaś ca
english: O you whose sight is never barren, if you would show favour to me, O lord, scorched by sorrow for my son, then by your grace let my dead son live again this day, and let me be joined with him once more.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca yas te putro dayito 'yaṃ viyātaḥ; svarṇaṣṭhīvī yam adāt parvatas te punas te taṃ putram ahaṃ dadāmi; hiraṇyanābhaṃ varṣasahasriṇaṃ ca
english: Nārada said: That dear son of yours who has passed away — the Gold-Spitter whom Parvata granted you — that very son I now give back to you again, Hiraṇyanābha, endowed once more with a span of a thousand years.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca sa kathaṃ kāñcanaṣṭhīvī sṛñjayasya suto 'bhavat parvatena kimarthaṃ ca dattaḥ kena mamāra ca
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: How did the son of Sṛñjaya come to be the Gold-Spitter? For what reason was he granted by Parvata, and by what cause did he die?

sanskrit: yadā varṣasahasrāyus tadā bhavati mānavaḥ katham aprāptakaumāraḥ sṛñjayasya suto mṛtaḥ
english: If a man's allotted span was a thousand years, how then did Sṛñjaya's son die before he had even reached his boyhood?

sanskrit: utāho nāmamātraṃ vai suvarṇaṣṭhīvino 'bhavat tathyaṃ vā kāñcanaṣṭhīvīty etad icchāmi veditum
english: Was "Gold-Spitter" but a name only, or was it truly so that he spat gold? This I wish to learn.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca atra te kathayiṣyāmi yathā vṛttaṃ janeśvara nāradaḥ parvataś caiva prāg ṛṣī lokapūjitau
english: Vāsudeva said: I shall tell you how it came to pass, O lord of men. Long ago there were two seers, Nārada and Parvata, honoured throughout the worlds.

sanskrit: mātulo bhāgineyaś ca devalokād ihāgatau vihartukāmau saṃprītyā mānuṣyeṣu purā prabhū
english: Uncle and sister's son, those two mighty ones came down here of old from the world of the gods, wishing in their fondness to roam awhile among mortals.

sanskrit: haviḥpavitrabhojyena devabhojyena caiva ha nārado mātulaś caiva bhāgineyaś ca parvataḥ
english: On purifying oblation-food fit for sacrifice, and on the very fare of the gods, Nārada the uncle, and Parvata the sister's son, sustained themselves —

sanskrit: tāv ubhau tapasopetāv avanītalacāriṇau bhuñjānau mānuṣān bhogān yathāvat paryadhāvatām
english: both endowed with ascetic power, wandering over the surface of the earth, and tasting human pleasures, they ranged about as was fitting.

sanskrit: prītimantau mudā yuktau samayaṃ tatra cakratuḥ yo bhaved dhṛdi saṃkalpaḥ śubho vā yadi vāśubhaḥ anyonyasya sa ākhyeyo mṛṣā śāpo 'nyathā bhavet
english: Loving and joyful, they made there a compact: "Whatever resolve should arise in the heart, whether good or ill, it must be disclosed to the other; to do otherwise shall bring a curse upon the false one."

sanskrit: tau tatheti pratijñāya maharṣī lokapūjitau sṛñjayaṃ śvaityam abhyetya rājānam idam ūcatuḥ
english: "So be it," the two world-honoured great seers vowed; and coming to King Sṛñjaya, son of Śvitya, they said this to him:

sanskrit: āvāṃ bhavati vatsyāvaḥ kaṃ cit kālaṃ hitāya te yathāvat pṛthivīpāla āvayoḥ praguṇībhava tatheti kṛtvā tau rājā satkṛtyopacacāra ha
english: "We two shall dwell with you, sir, for a time, for your good; be duly attentive to us, O guardian of the earth." "So be it," said the king, and honouring them, he waited upon them well.

sanskrit: tataḥ kadā cit tau rājā mahātmānau tathāgatau abravīt paramaprītaḥ suteyaṃ varavarṇinī
english: Then one day, to those two great-souled ones who had so come to him, the king, exceedingly pleased, said: "This is my daughter, of fair complexion.

sanskrit: ekaiva mama kanyaiṣā yuvāṃ paricariṣyati darśanīyānavadyāṅgī śīlavṛttasamanvitā sukumārī kumārī ca padmakiñjalkasaṃnibhā
english: This is my one and only daughter, and she shall attend upon you both — lovely to look upon, flawless of limb, endowed with good character and conduct, tender and maidenly, and like the filament of a lotus."

sanskrit: paramaṃ saumya ity uktas tābhyāṃ rājā śaśāsa tām kanye viprāv upacara devavat pitṛvac ca ha
english: "Excellent, gentle one," said the two; and so addressed, the king commanded her: "Daughter, wait upon these brāhmaṇas as upon gods and as upon a father."

sanskrit: sā tu kanyā tathety uktvā pitaraṃ dharmacāriṇī yathānideśaṃ rājñas tau satkṛtyopacacāra ha
english: And that maiden, walking in righteousness, said "So be it" to her father, and according to the king's command she honoured the two and waited upon them.

sanskrit: tasyās tathopacāreṇa rūpeṇāpratimena ca nāradaṃ hṛcchayas tūrṇaṃ sahasaivānvapadyata
english: By her ministering thus, and by her matchless beauty, love swiftly and all at once took hold of Nārada's heart.

sanskrit: vavṛdhe ca tatas tasya hṛdi kāmo mahātmanaḥ yathā śuklasya pakṣasya pravṛttāv uḍurāṭ chanaiḥ
english: And then desire grew in the heart of that great-souled one, as the lord of the stars, the moon, waxes slowly at the onset of the bright fortnight.

sanskrit: na ca taṃ bhāgineyāya parvatāya mahātmane śaśaṃsa manmathaṃ tīvraṃ vrīḍamānaḥ sa dharmavit
english: Yet that knower of the law, out of shame, did not disclose his fierce passion to his sister's son, the great-souled Parvata.

sanskrit: tapasā ceṅgitenātha parvato 'tha bubodha tat kāmārtaṃ nāradaṃ kruddhaḥ śaśāpainaṃ tato bhṛśam
english: But by his ascetic power and by Nārada's bearing, Parvata came to know it; and in anger at Nārada, stricken with desire, he then cursed him bitterly.

sanskrit: kṛtvā samayam avyagro bhavān vai sahito mayā yo bhaved dhṛdi saṃkalpaḥ śubho vā yadi vāśubhaḥ
english: "You made a compact with me without reservation: that whatever resolve should arise in the heart, whether good or ill,

sanskrit: anyonyasya sa ākhyeya iti tad vai mṛṣā kṛtam bhavatā vacanaṃ brahmaṃs tasmād etad vadāmy aham
english: it should be disclosed to one another. That word of yours, O brāhmaṇa, you have made false; and therefore I say this to you.

sanskrit: na hi kāmaṃ pravartantaṃ bhavān ācaṣṭa me purā sukumāryāṃ kumāryāṃ te tasmād eṣa śapāmy aham
english: You did not tell me earlier of the desire stirring within you for the maiden Sukumārī; for that reason I now lay this curse upon you.

sanskrit: brahmavādī gurur yasmāt tapasvī brāhmaṇaś ca san akārṣīḥ samayabhraṃśam āvābhyāṃ yaḥ kṛto mithaḥ
english: Since you, a teacher and an expounder of the sacred word, an ascetic and a brāhmaṇa, have broken the compact made between us two —

sanskrit: śapsye tasmāt susaṃkruddho bhavantaṃ taṃ nibodha me sukumārī ca te bhāryā bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ
english: therefore, in deep wrath, I shall curse you; hear me. Sukumārī shall indeed become your wife — of that there is no doubt;

sanskrit: vānaraṃ caiva kanyā tvāṃ vivāhāt prabhṛti prabho saṃdrakṣyanti narāś cānye svarūpeṇa vinākṛtam
english: but from the moment of the wedding onward, O lord, the maiden — and other men besides — shall behold you as a monkey, stripped of your own form."

sanskrit: sa tad vākyaṃ tu vijñāya nāradaḥ parvatāt tadā aśapat tam api krodhād bhāgineyaṃ sa mātulaḥ
english: And when Nārada had heard that speech from Parvata, then the uncle in his turn cursed his sister's son in anger:

sanskrit: tapasā brahmacaryeṇa satyena ca damena ca yukto 'pi dharmanityaś ca na svargavāsam āpsyasi
english: "Though endowed with austerity, with chastity, with truth, and with self-restraint, and ever devoted to righteousness, you shall not attain a dwelling in heaven."

sanskrit: tau tu śaptvā bhṛśaṃ kruddhau parasparam amarṣaṇau pratijagmatur anyonyaṃ kruddhāv iva gajottamau
english: Having cursed each other thus, in deep wrath and intolerant of one another, the two parted ways, like a pair of mighty elephants enraged.

sanskrit: parvataḥ pṛthivīṃ kṛtsnāṃ vicacāra mahāmuniḥ pūjyamāno yathānyāyaṃ tejasā svena bhārata
english: Parvata, the great sage, wandered over the whole earth, honoured everywhere as was his due by his own splendour, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: atha tām alabhat kanyāṃ nāradaḥ sṛñjayātmajām dharmeṇa dharmapravaraḥ sukumārīm aninditām
english: Then Nārada, foremost in righteousness, lawfully won that maiden, the blameless Sukumārī, the daughter of Sṛñjaya.

sanskrit: sā tu kanyā yathāśāpaṃ nāradaṃ taṃ dadarśa ha pāṇigrahaṇamantrāṇāṃ prayogād eva vānaram
english: But that maiden, in accordance with the curse, beheld Nārada — from the very moment the marriage-mantras were pronounced — as a monkey.

sanskrit: sukumārī ca devarṣiṃ vānarapratimānanam naivāvamanyata tadā prītimaty eva cābhavat
english: Yet Sukumārī did not scorn the divine seer, monkey-faced though he was; on the contrary, she remained full of affection for him.

sanskrit: upatasthe ca bhartāraṃ na cānyaṃ manasāpy agāt devaṃ muniṃ vā yakṣaṃ vā patitve pativatsalā
english: Devoted to her husband, she waited upon him and did not, even in thought, turn to another — neither god, nor sage, nor yakṣa — to take as her lord.

sanskrit: tataḥ kadā cid bhagavān parvato 'nusasāra ha vanaṃ virahitaṃ kiṃ cit tatrāpaśyat sa nāradam
english: Then once the venerable Parvata went into a certain solitary forest, and there he caught sight of Nārada.

sanskrit: tato 'bhivādya provāca nāradaṃ parvatas tadā bhavān prasādaṃ kurutāṃ svargādeśāya me prabho
english: Then, having saluted him, Parvata said to Nārada: "Be gracious to me, O lord, and grant me leave to enter heaven."

sanskrit: tam uvāca tato dṛṣṭvā parvataṃ nāradas tadā kṛtāñjalim upāsīnaṃ dīnaṃ dīnataraḥ svayam
english: Then Nārada, beholding Parvata seated before him with hands folded in supplication and downcast — himself yet more downcast — said to him:

sanskrit: tvayāhaṃ prathamaṃ śapto vānaras tvaṃ bhaviṣyasi ity uktena mayā paścāc chaptas tvam api matsarāt adyaprabhṛti vai vāsaṃ svarge nāvāpsyasīti ha
english: "You first cursed me, saying, 'You shall become a monkey'; and afterward, stung by resentment, I cursed you too, saying, 'From this day forth you shall not attain a dwelling in heaven.'

sanskrit: tava naitad dhi sadṛśaṃ putrasthāne hi me bhavān nivartayetāṃ tau śāpam anyo 'nyena tadā munī
english: This is not worthy of you, for you stand to me in the place of a son." And so the two sages then withdrew, each from the other, the curses they had laid.

sanskrit: śrīsamṛddhaṃ tadā dṛṣṭvā nāradaṃ devarūpiṇam sukumārī pradudrāva parapaty abhiśaṅkayā
english: Then, seeing Nārada radiant with glory and of godlike form, Sukumārī fled, fearing he must be some other woman's husband.

sanskrit: tāṃ parvatas tato dṛṣṭvā pradravantīm aninditām abravīt tava bhartaiṣa nātra kāryā vicāraṇā
english: Then Parvata, seeing the blameless one fleeing, said to her: "This is your own husband; there is no need to doubt it here.

sanskrit: ṛṣiḥ paramadharmātmā nārado bhagavān prabhuḥ tavaivābhedyahṛdayo mā te bhūd atra saṃśayaḥ
english: The seer Nārada, the venerable lord, a soul supremely righteous, is yours alone, his heart cleaving to none but you. Let there be no doubt of this in your mind."

sanskrit: sānunītā bahuvidhaṃ parvatena mahātmanā śāpadoṣaṃ ca taṃ bhartuḥ śrutvā svāṃ prakṛtiṃ gatā parvato 'tha yayau svargaṃ nārado 'tha yayau gṛhān
english: Reassured in many ways by the great-souled Parvata, and having heard of that taint of the curse upon her husband, she returned to her own nature; then Parvata went to heaven, and Nārada went to his home.

sanskrit: pratyakṣakarmā sarvasya nārado 'yaṃ mahān ṛṣiḥ eṣa vakṣyati vai pṛṣṭo yathā vṛttaṃ narottama
english: This great seer Nārada, before whose eyes all things are made manifest, will himself, if asked, tell you how it came to pass, O best of men.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato rājā pāṇḍusuto nāradaṃ pratyabhāṣata bhagavañ śrotum icchāmi suvarṇaṣṭhīvisaṃbhavam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the king, the son of Pāṇḍu, replied to Nārada: "Venerable one, I wish to hear of the origin of the Gold-Spitter."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sa ca munir dharmarājena nāradaḥ ācacakṣe yathā vṛttaṃ suvarṇaṣṭhīvinaṃ prati
english: So addressed by the King of Righteousness, the sage Nārada recounted how it had come to pass concerning the Gold-Spitter.

sanskrit: evam etan mahārāja yathāyaṃ keśavo 'bravīt kāryasyāsya tu yac cheṣaṃ tat te vakṣyāmi pṛcchataḥ
english: "It is even so, O great king, as Keśava has told it. But what remains of this matter, that I shall relate to you, since you ask.

sanskrit: ahaṃ ca parvataś caiva svasrīyo me mahāmuniḥ vastukāmāv abhigatau sṛñjayaṃ jayatāṃ varam
english: I and Parvata — my sister's son, the great sage — wishing for lodging, came to Sṛñjaya, the best of the victorious.

sanskrit: tatra saṃpūjitau tena vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā sarvakāmaiḥ suvihitau nivasāvo 'sya veśmani
english: There, honoured by him with rites prescribed by ordinance, and well provided with every comfort, we dwelt in his house.

sanskrit: vyatikrāntāsu varṣāsu samaye gamanasya ca parvato mām uvācedaṃ kāle vacanam arthavat
english: When the rains had passed and the time for departure was at hand, Parvata spoke to me these words, weighty and timely:

sanskrit: āvām asya narendrasya gṛhe paramapūjitau uṣitau samaye brahmaṃś cintyatām atra sāṃpratam
english: "We two have dwelt, most highly honoured, in the house of this lord of men for the appointed time. Now, O brāhmaṇa, let us take thought what should be done in return."

sanskrit: tato 'ham abruvaṃ rājan parvataṃ śubhadarśanam sarvam etat tvayi vibho bhāgineyopapadyate
english: Then I said, O king, to the fair-seeming Parvata: "All this rests with you, my lord, my sister's son.

sanskrit: vareṇa chandyatāṃ rājā labhatāṃ yad yad icchati āvayos tapasā siddhiṃ prāpnotu yadi manyase
english: Let the king be offered a boon and obtain whatever he desires; by the power of our austerities let him gain his wish, if you think it fitting."

sanskrit: tata āhūya rājānaṃ sṛñjayaṃ śubhadarśanam parvato 'numataṃ vākyam uvāca munipuṃgavaḥ
english: Then Parvata, the bull among sages, summoned the fair-seeming King Sṛñjaya and spoke these agreed-upon words:

sanskrit: prītau svo nṛpa satkārais tava hy ārjavasaṃbhṛtaiḥ āvābhyām abhyanujñāto varaṃ nṛvara cintaya
english: "We two are pleased, O king, with the honours you have rendered us, born of your sincerity. With our leave, O best of men, think now upon a boon.

sanskrit: devānām avihiṃsāyāṃ yad bhaven mānuṣakṣamam tad gṛhāṇa mahārāja pūjārho nau mato bhavān
english: Whatever, without offence to the gods, lies within the measure of what is possible for a mortal, that take, O great king; for you are deemed by us worthy of honour."

sanskrit: sṛñjaya uvāca prītau bhavantau yadi me kṛtam etāvatā mama eṣa eva paro lābho nirvṛtto me mahāphalaḥ
english: Sṛñjaya said: If you two are pleased with me, then by that alone my purpose is achieved; this very thing is for me the highest gain, attained and rich in fruit.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca tam evaṃvādinaṃ bhūyaḥ parvataḥ pratyabhāṣata vṛṇīṣva rājan saṃkalpo yas te hṛdi ciraṃ sthitaḥ
english: Nārada said: To him, who spoke thus, Parvata replied once more: "Choose, O king, the desire that has long abided in your heart."

sanskrit: sṛñjaya uvāca abhīpsāmi sutaṃ vīraṃ vīryavantaṃ dṛḍhavratam āyuṣmantaṃ mahābhāgaṃ devarājasamadyutim
english: Sṛñjaya said: I long for a son — a hero, valiant and firm in his vows, long-lived and greatly blessed, splendid as the king of the gods.

sanskrit: parvata uvāca bhaviṣyaty eṣa te kāmo na tv āyuṣmān bhaviṣyati devarājābhibhūtyarthaṃ saṃkalpo hy eṣa te hṛdi
english: Parvata said: This desire of yours shall be fulfilled, but he shall not be long-lived; for this resolve in your heart is meant to surpass the king of the gods.

sanskrit: suvarṇaṣṭhīvanāc caiva svarṇaṣṭhīvī bhaviṣyati rakṣyaś ca devarājāt sa devarājasamadyutiḥ
english: And from his spitting of gold he shall become the Gold-Spitter; and he, splendid as the king of the gods, must be guarded against the king of the gods.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca tac chrutvā sṛñjayo vākyaṃ parvatasya mahātmanaḥ prasādayām āsa tadā naitad evaṃ bhaved iti
english: Nārada said: Having heard this speech of the great-souled Parvata, Sṛñjaya then sought to win him over, saying, "Let it not be thus."

sanskrit: āyuṣmān me bhavet putro bhavatas tapasā mune na ca taṃ parvataḥ kiṃ cid uvācendravyapekṣayā
english: "Let my son be long-lived, O sage, by the power of your austerity." But Parvata said nothing at all to him in reply, out of regard for Indra.

sanskrit: tam ahaṃ nṛpatiṃ dīnam abruvaṃ punar eva tu smartavyo 'haṃ mahārāja darśayiṣyāmi te smṛtaḥ
english: To that grieving king I then spoke once again: "Remember me, O great king; when remembered, I shall show myself to you."
